Senses.Explanation: Literally, "brows intertwined with one another." The phrase occurs 129 times in 80 allowlisted texts. The records use the bodily image for persons brought into exceptionally close conjunction: one master says that for five or six years he has had his brows intertwined with the assembly, yet in fact they have had "no traffic in rice or water" (五六年來雖則與諸人眉毛廝結，其實水米無交). Another requires "brows intertwined, sharing life and sharing death" (眉毛廝結，同生同死). It also appears as an answer in a public interview: asked for the phrase for opening the retreat, the master replies, "brows intertwined" (眉毛廝結). Elsewhere a hall address sets saying and silence against each other: "if one speaks, heaven and earth are far apart; if one does not speak, brows are intertwined" (說即天地懸殊，不說即眉毛廝結). The Chan use turns a physical impossibility into a compact, repeatable encounter phrase; the accompanying clauses establish proximity or conjunction but do not authorize this entry to decide what speakers intend by it.
Senses.Note: One idiomatic referent covers the sampled uses. Pairings with “no dealings,” “sharing life and death,” speech/silence, and retreat opening are distinct contexts, not distinct objects or word classes. No second sense is created from competing readings of the image.

Occurrences.Kwic: 五六年來雖則與諸人眉毛廝結，其實水米無交
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 列祖提綱錄, Liao'an Qingyu's sequence of winter-solstice informal addresses. Liao'an is the exact speaker who says that for five or six years he and the assembly have intertwined eyebrows while in fact having no exchange of water or rice.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直須眉毛廝結，同生同死。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 列祖提綱錄 explicitly introduces Ying'an Tanhua's arrival address at Changlu. Ying'an is the exact speaker who says that merely seeing the banner across the river is insufficient and that one must intertwine eyebrows, living and dying together.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「摩竭掩室、毘耶杜口則不問，即今天童結制一句，請師舉唱。」師云：「眉毛廝結。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 費隱禪師語錄, opening-the-furnace public interview. Feiyin Tongrong is the exact speaker: an unnamed monk requests a phrase for the Tiantong retreat, and Feiyin answers 'eyebrows knit together.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 說即天地懸殊，不說即眉毛廝結。說與不說，拈放一邊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷). Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書), Huguo Zhizhuan section. Huguo Zhizhuan is the exact hall speaker who says that speaking makes heaven and earth hang far apart while not speaking makes the eyebrows knit together.
